definition: requests per second returning 2xx with slowdown <= threshold, where slowdown = ttlt_ms / baseline_service_ms (the request's own required service time). 429/503 count as offered-and-failed with zero useful completion, never as zero-latency samples.
basis: Both thresholds from stock FCFS in the saturated round-A run, which predates every arm they judge. TIGHT is its median slowdown, LAX its p95. Both are reported side by side because the choice moves the verdict.
frozen_before: the overload arm (C') and any 15 ms contract arm (B)
reporting_rule: goodput at both thresholds, side by side, with the rejection rate and the status breakdown that produced it
why_not_absolute_ttlt: v1 fixed absolute TTLT cutoffs, which is wrong for this workload: a request generating thousands of tokens cannot meet a 2.2 s bound however well it is scheduled, so an absolute cutoff conflates queued-too-long with intrinsically-long, and shedding long requests would fake a goodput gain. Slowdown judges each request against its own service time.
